# Synthetic ELF fixtures for crates/loader.
# Generated by `cargo run -p kat-gen -- loader`. Do not edit.
#
# Hand-built rather than compiled: no RV32 toolchain will emit most of
# these, and a fixture that is 100 bytes long is one a reviewer can read
# in full. `minimal.elf` is the shape they all deviate from.
#
# Fields: file name, sha256 of the file, what it is.

et_rel.elf 7ea8cd4eee19669b56a95fb56eccd23408e54a2a3d7a80b5c369f46a29cc092b e_type = ET_REL: a relocatable object, which is not a program
instruction_too_long.elf 2697e1adbbc4c8f2446e6fd53be57826e12a8e4505c98f9d5fa224863429cd9f 0x0000_001f: bits 4:2 all ones, so a 48-bit encoding
minimal.elf 7d306fc27e3af73f1bac562c8754e5c69893b8d280cc3e174a1f7ad756eeb752 a valid one-segment RV32 executable: the positive control for every negative below, and proof that the builder itself is right

zcmp.elf ff7fd5bd53f1acdd515ea51b6002c2dc24bb4dbda987a987dceaee904caecb4e 0xb872, a cm.push-shaped halfword in quadrant 2 funct3 = 101: the Zcmp encoding space, which RV32IMAC does not have
zero_halfword.elf d83bf8ca5ab9b40ae595129404a797e8f5c9a23fbd247e4f6aba166496d2db5e an all-zero halfword after a c.nop: RVC's defined-illegal encoding, which the sweep records as not code rather than refusing -- this one is a positive fixture, not a negative
zero_halfword_run.elf c254aaa206d3e893673c82cacb1037024cbc8e10d717b4eca233714ee1f26b1c c.nop, two all-zero halfwords, c.jr ra, one more, c.nop: the sweep must resynchronise on the far side of padding rather than swallow what follows it. The lone halfword is the load-bearing one -- after a pair, a sweep that over-advanced by two bytes would land on the second and look correct, because an unswept slot is already NonInstruction
